description: Very large stitched collage of roughly 100+ mainstream and online news headlines/screenshots about QAnon, apparently assembled to show the volume of media coverage of the movement circa August 2019. Outlets include Newsweek, The New York Times, The Washington Post, The Guardian, Mother Jones, Rolling Stone, The Daily Beast, The Daily Dot, The Hill, BuzzFeed News, The Verge, Vox, Forbes, MSNBC, Raw Story, ThinkProgress, The Week, The Nation and many foreign-language outlets. Recurring themes: the FBI designating QAnon-related conspiracy theories a domestic terrorism threat, 8chan's shutdown, Trump rallies and campaign ads featuring QAnon signs, Chrissy Teigen, the Epoch Times, and platform bans/censorship.

description: Cropped scan of a typewritten paragraph (numbered 5) from a formerly classified document discussing 'the Agency's posture toward the media,' describing it as defensive, reactive and tongue-tied, and suggesting it may be time for an offense to get things in better balance. Marked 'All portions are classified SECRET' with a SECRET stamp. The wording ('the Agency') is consistent with a declassified CIA internal memo on media relations, though the document is not otherwise identified in the crop.
text: 5. The Agency's posture toward the media is basically defensive, reactive and tongue-tied. What we say is: "no comment"; "that disclosure was wrong and outrageous." Next we wring our hands, send emissaries out to brief key people in the Administration and Congress and correct the record, then hunker back awaiting the next blow. Maybe it's time for an offense as well as a defense and an attempt to get things in better balance. Here are some personal thoughts as to do's and don'ts on this score. All portions are classified SECRET. SECRET.
